conclusions: Original training wording improves thinking F21 to24 and R69 to73; original development scores are unchanged.
Thinking F improvements4, loss1 and5 wrong both demonstrate mixed wording-sensitive and persistent errors under the tested forms; not development wording alone.
Nonthinking F stays27/30; nonthinking R79 to81. All42 controls and1440 filler records exactly match, and target format/cap/boundary errors are zero.
Wrong thinking training outputs often select another book/author association. Visible trace text does not prove a causal internal mechanism or absent knowledge.
Full M1 still fails original dev gate. No new acceptance verdict, best-mode selection, new budget, dataset rewrite or canonical promotion.

Next: prospectively choose a bounded SFT improvement for reverse-association reliability/generalization across all F/R, preserving current failed control/gates/final-test isolation. Exact intervention/budget is not selected in this review.
Cross-mode comparisons also differ in greedy versus sampled decoding/token budget; within-mode wording comparisons retain their own fixed policies. Do not identify a pure causal thinking-mode effect.

candidate_next_intervention.proposal: Test explicit inverse prize-to-book support across all F/R while preserving existing task/gate evaluation.
candidate_next_intervention.rationale: The current seven-task set has direct book-to-prize and book-to-author but no standalone prize-to-book task; remaining wrong thinking traces often bind the prize to another learned book/author. This is a proposed training intervention, not an established mechanism or guaranteed remedy.
